Kingston 8 GB Class 4 SDHC Flash Memory Card SD4/8GB I ordered this part for use with a new Audibon Birdcam. The Kingston memory card failed in just over a month. It was unreadable by several PCs and a Mac. Amazon said to contact Kingston directly (Kingston memories carry a lifetime warranty). Kingston had me return the memory (my expense) and issued an RMA. They used "UPS Mail Innovations" to ship.
UPS MI is an el-cheapo service that uses the USPS mid-stream and for final delivery. Predictably, the shipment to me was lost by the USPS and tracking information abruptly stopped. It took four telephone calls to Kingston, the final call being to a supervisor, to get another parts shipped. The CS reps kept reading me the dead tracking info in which the shipment was "out for delivery" in another state and past due by several days. It's been three weeks since I sent the part back. I'm waiting for the second RMA part to arrive.
I'm not sure that Sandisk memories are fundamentally any better, but I can say that I never suffered a failure of any of their many memories I own.
text_fidelity_b: Kingston 8 GB Class 4 SDHC Flash Memory Card SD4/8GB

text_fidelity_a:
Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN) DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. I am a Centurylink/Qwest customer of over 25 years. I have a old Actiontec Q1000 router/modem. My DSL Ethernet connection to my desk top has gone down for hours at a time lately. My wifi goes out 10-12 times daily as of late. Small one story house with only two old, non gamer people with latest model $800 smart phones. I read the online instructions and even watched Actiontec video for installing this product. I had a problem and called 1-888-436-0657 the tech support number listed in the Quick Start Guide. Actiontec's phone answering tree makes it very clear that they will not provide any tech support for products purchased from Amazon or any other "unauthorized dealers". I pressed 0 and they hung up on me three seperate times. The Amazon listing for this product made it very clear that it would work with Centturylink. It has a big check mark for Centurylink.

I have spent so many hours on the phone, through email and chat mode with Centurylink it is embarrassing. I offered to pay Centurylink to have a tech come to my home and install my new router/modem. Centurylink said their techs were not allowed to install router/modems but would check my outside wiring for free and my inside wiring for $85 minimun. Centurylink told me they would be happy to have a tech walk me through my hookup via telephone. After I finally was connected to a Centurylink tech and was verified they advised me they were not "allowed" to offer tech support to their customers on this product. They made it sound like it was a federal felony to offer tech support on this product.

Best Buy in New Mexico, and apparently all other retailers no longer carry any products compatible with Centurylink DSL because of their refusal to offer tech support. I heard that Amazon is having so many issues with router/modems that they are reluctant to take returns. I guess I will be taking the $67 loss. I should have rememberd my latin "caveat emptor".

So now I am going to angrily switch to the second most hated consumer corporation, Xfinity. Did you know that Xfinity is Comcast with a new name? Comcast's reputation is so trashed they decided if they adopted a new name they could fool a lot of consumers. As we all know, there is no real free market with open competition. In most markets you have DSL with the only telephone company available or cable with the only cable company in your neighborhood. A pig with lipstick is still, after all just a pig. I am advising myself and everyone else to do serious due diligence before purchasing any internet electronics from any vendors. Or you could just rent the overpriced and low quality products peddled by the ISPs.
text_fidelity_b: Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer) I have owned these headphones since August, 2014. They are easy to use, and the sound quality is excellent. Prior to owning them, I tried out some $20 wireless headphones from a local drugstore which did not work at all, and I also did a jury-rigged setup with a very long, trip-hazard cable linking some headphones I owned to my TiVo. Never again. Both were a disaster.

This system is absolutely wonderful for two reasons:

First, I have weird hearing issues in that when I am trying to sleep, every little sound bugs me and I seem to hear even a conversation in the next room far more clearly than I have any desire to do, but when listening to TV, I can't understand 75% of what the actors are saying without captions. Go figure. With these headphones, no more problem. All dialog is clear as a bell.

Second, I no longer have to drive my husband crazy blaring the TV in order to adequately hear the actors speaking. By the same token, if my husband is watching a program on TV that I'm not at all interested in, I don't have to be subjected to listening to that either.

It's win-win.

I will say that I was not myself techie enough to install these headphones. My husband is an IT guy and he had to do it for me. So that's one downside for the customer who struggles with techie installations. Other than that, all is great.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver) I've been thinking about upgrading from my Canon 50d for awhile now. I thought I wanted a full frame camera, but I could never justify spending that kind of money on a hobby. One of the main reasons was that I had sort of got out of the habit of shooting as much as I used. Part of the reason was that it always seemed like such a pain to lug around the camera. There were always times I wish I had a camera, but didn't.

This camera solves a lot of that for me. Take the lens off the body and the thing literally fits in your pocket. Leave it on and it fits nicely in my car's center console. It feels nice in my hands, although I bought the metal thumb grip at the same time as the camera and must admit that does help quite a bit.

Compared to my 50d (which is a little long in the tooth) the image quality is superior. The color reproduction in particular seemed to be good. It also seemed to perform better at higher ISOs than my 50d does. Really, the only area where the 50d still out-performs the XE-2 is how fast the autofocus works. The XE-2 is good, but my 50d is still a touch better. Maybe a firmware update will improve this.

Despite using a Canon products for almost a decade, I found I really like the controls on this camera. I found it really easy and intuitive to change the shutter speed and aperature. ISO and most of the other frequently used settings are easily reached by hitting the Q button. The layout could be tweaked a little, but overall it's pretty good.

I've never had a camera with wifi, but it's a feature that's gotten more use than I thought it would. Being able to transmit pictures to Facebook, Twitter, or whatever is really simple once you upload the photo from the camera using Fuji's app. I don't post a lot of pictures online, but that may change a little bit now that it is a lot simpler.

The build quality is really good and the included kit lens is really nice. The screen is sharp and the EVF is clear. Like I mentioned before, the size of the frame is nice and compact and is much easier to take along wherever you go.

Is this a replacement for a full frame DSLR? No. Is it a good alternative for a crop sensor DSLR? In my opinion, absolutely. First, the price and performance makes it very competitive. Second, the size is going to be tough to beat. Finally, for me at least, it is a camera I am more likely to use more and take with me more places. As other's have mentioned about this camera though, if you like putting everything on automatic or different shooting modes (sports, portrait, landscape, etc) then this camera is probably not for you. If you are interested in learning how to shoot without those crutches, this camera would be a great place to start.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver)

Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design. I bought this keyboard as a replacement for the original one came with my HP computer which is a USB wireless. I liked the original one but it can't be used with rechargeable AA for a long time. I had to keep recharging constantly. And I didn't like the idea of wasting throw away batteries.
This new keyboard is just as compact and light as the original, it's a minimalist's dream. Key stroke is very quiet and requires very short stroke kind of like using a notepad keyboard. Plug & play operation is extremely trouble free, you'll need no instruction at all. Some of the photos I have seen showing PS2(old type connection) adaptor included but mine didn't include it, which wasn't an issue for me. There's a special key for "calc" but I didn't have a problem starting it in a couple of key strokes, so it's not a big advantage. Another feature is its "spill-resistant design". It's nothing more than a several slits under the keyboard. If you spill water, it may help drying quicker, for anything else, you'll have a hard time getting it clean, probably never completely like any other keyboard.
Over all, I like everything about this keyboard with no negative opinion. Only thing I don't know about it is its durability but from the way I feel, it seems well made and will last for a long time.
The photo showing on this page is misleading. It comes with keyboard only without a mouse.

text_fidelity_a: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) The new Kindle arrived within 2 days of my order. I sat down and played around with it for a few minutes and learned the icons but that's all that can be done until it is registered with Amazon. I took it to Toyota while getting my car serviced. Our local Toyota dealer has free WiFi for customers. The Kindle found the hot spot and Amazon recognized the Kindle right away.  It took a few taps around the screen to get started but was easy with a little exploring. Within the time to get an oil change, I had downloaded my ebooks from Cloud and even bought a nice app on sale.  Next I stopped by BestBuy and added a Kindle micro USB to USB cable.  The cable can be used to download ebooks from your PC when not connected to wireless.  Using free Calibre to manage the free ebooks from the Internet, enables covers and metadata for those ebooks that have none.  Calibre will also download the books to Kindle from a PC.  The Fire is great but took some thinking and patience to get it to do all the things I imagined it would do. For instance, ebooks without covers will all look alike and have no title.  This is why it is important to use Calibre for ebook management. Reading ebooks is so much better than it was 10 years ago and this is only the beginning.  The download speed is great.  The reading speed is also great.The storage space is really more than enough.  The 8 Gigabytes of memory is close to 2 warehouses of data. text_fidelity_a:
HP 20-inch LED (1600 X 900) LED Backlit Monitor with VGA & DVI-D Port (W2082a, Black) - L8K84AA#ABA This is a decent PC monitor that doesn’t excel in any area but, at the same time, doesn’t fall flat either (except for sound quality). It’s a good choice if you’re looking for an inexpensive, wide-screen monitor that comes in at under $100.

The build quality is what you’d expect at this price point: pretty basic and simple. The casing is all plastic, and rather cheap feeling plastic at that. It comes with a very basic stand that allows a limited amount of tilt adjustment, but no swivel or monitor rotation. There are no mounting holes on the back to facilitate a wall or stand mount. There are also no convenience features, such as a USB hub. It also lacks an HDMI port.

On the plus side, the power cord just plugs into the monitor without the need for a transformer or wall wart. The overall monitor profile is pretty slim, and it is very lightweight.

Setup is very simple. No tools are needed to attach the stand (just push and it clicks into place). It comes with a VGA cable, a 3.5mm audio cable and a power cable. Although it includes a DVI port, it does not come with the cable to use that. It also does not come with a user guide (other than a one-page quick setup sheet) or a driver disk. Both are available as downloads from the HP site. However, neither are really needed.

I hooked it up to my laptop via VGA to use as a secondary monitor. It auto installed under Win 7, so it should be able to do the same for 8 and 10. The recommended resolution is 1600x900 at 60Htz.

Right out of the box the settings were eye-searing bright, as is typical with manufacturer defaults since they want their monitors to stand out when on display in a store. Changing the settings is pretty easy – the menu button brings up the full list of options; you select the one you want; then adjust with the +/- keys. You can experiment at will since there’s also a choice to return to factory defaults should you get lost in the weeds with changes. The adjustment menu is pretty extensive for a monitor at this price point. You can adjust the usual brightness and contrast, and also color temp, image control, and even turn off the blue LED power indicator (yes!). Unfortunately, the control button labels are impossible to read (black on black) but there’s only a few buttons, so it's not tough to figure out.

The image quality is decent once it’s been properly adjusted. It won’t wow you, but it provides good performance on both images and text. I was happier with the text performance than I was with video (it has pretty limited black levels) but, for an everyday, inexpensive monitor, it’s more than acceptable.

The speakers are very, very basic. Tinny to the point of being useless. I’ve gotten better sound out of a $5 set of basic computer speakers.

I’m giving this 4 stars since, even at this price point, HP could have done a better job with the overall look/feel of the monitor, have included some additional convenience features such as a swivel, USB hub, and/or an HDMI port. Features that could have been dropped are the internal speakers, which are useless for anything other than to hear system beeps. Still, even as-is, it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a no-frills, no-fuss, inexpensive monitor.
text_fidelity_b: HP 20-inch LED (1600 X 900) LED Backlit Monitor with VGA & DVI-D Port (W2082a, Black) - L8K84AA#ABA

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging The frustration free packaging is a big plus.
The mount itself is perfect for our needs.
We have a Garmin Nuvi which came with the window suction mount. The window mount has a ball-joint the same as this friction mount.
The GPS came with the clip-on bracket which has the socket attached which then clips onto the ball on this friction mount.
This forms a multi-directional ball and socket joint allowing for easy angle adjustments.

This mount has stayed in place with no problems, even when we've armorall'ed the dashboard. Then again, we don't fling the truck around like teenagers either, the worst we do is bounce it around on some dirt roads.

We much prefer this over the window mount for several reasons:
We live in Georgia (USA) and the heat and the humidity in summer takes its toll on the sucker attachments on the window mounts.
For security, we move the GPS from sight whenever we park.... the whole unit is easily picked up and placed on the floor.
We couldn't do this with a window mount. We either unclipped and left the mount attached to the window, a visible tell-tale that there's a GPS in the vehicle. Or, we would fiddle to remove the whole mount from the window (never too easy), and then are left with a tell-tale suction scum ring on the window! ...once more telling would-be GPS thieves that there's a GPS in the car! And that scum ring is just unsightly. Yes, you can get wipes... but this is a far more elegant solution and much more convenient.
Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Taken for what this is supposed to be, this is a fabulous machine. It's not a primary computer. It's not a laptop replacement. If you need a low power/ultra-portable computer, go with a netbook.

This is more of a mutt. It's a portable media player that doesn't have as much storage as an iPod or a Zen, but has a larger, higher quality screen and a kickstand, which makes it easier to watch movies at a desk.

It can read ebooks. It's not quite as light or comfortable for long term reading as a Kindle, but it can support full color images. It's far superior for this purpose than any of the other devices Amazon has put out an app for.

It can run Windows 7. It's not a full powered machine, but it's even smaller than a netbook.

It fits a slot somewhere between a PDA/smartphone and a netbook, and it's brilliant.

I would have liked a larger hard drive, an SD card (it would have gotten 5 stars if it had one) and more than one USB slot. There is no ethernet port. It only connects wirelessly. The optional port replicator gives you Ethernet and two more USB slots, but still no SD.

A few things to keep in mind. When you're first setting it up, you can't access the virtual keyboard button, so you need to use the Ease of Access icon to get to that. Windows will say to press the space bar to activate the feature. Use the mouse click button (marked +).

The design is very sleek. It's comfortable to hold and work with. The screen has an adjustable brightness, which is easier on the eyes, and easier to use in bright sunlight. The low glare screen helps with this as well.

Overall, this is bleeding edge, early adopter technology.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

Philips SPP4105B/17 10-Outlet Home Office Surge Protector (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The outlets are spaced so that the larger plugs don't block multiple slots. There is plenty of room, even for the large ones.

Rather than trickling out power to devices that aren't on, the system automatically shuts down power to the energy saving outlet when the main outlet is shut off. This is great if the energy savers are peripherals and the main is a PC, but if you're doing something other than a computer setup it can be a pain to remember to only plug an "always on" device into this slot. If you shut that device off, everything in the 7 energy saving outlets will lose power. The power loss will trigger if you reboot your machine, which means that all of your peripherals will go through a full boot cycle as well.

I'd have preferred a switch to enable or disable this feature, and an outlet for charging USB devices rather than coax.

Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case These headphones are advertised more for business use than for music. The business features do work great. There is a bluetooth adapter included in the package so you can use the headphones with PCs that don't have built-in bluetooth. You can connect the headphones to 2 different bluetooth sources simultaneously so you can have a Skype call on your laptop and connect to your smartphone at the same time. There is a nice pass-through mode that lets you listen to your surroundings (or not) by pushing a button on the Jabra app.

Speaking of the app, the included manual is very skimpy and really unnecessary. To use these headphones you should download the Jabra app to your phone or PC and use the app to pair and configure the headphones. Many of the features are only available through the app.

Sound quality of the headphone is great for business use, very solid with no connection problems. For music, this is not the best I have heard from "true wireless" headphones. Some music-focused "true wireless" headphones that I own have better clarity and detail. The Jabra app does have an equalizer feature, but the effect is more subtle than what I get from other headphones.

These headphones are very comfortable and very secure, actually surprisingly secure for headphones that don't have any wings or clips. 3 different size ear tips are included, though no memory foam tips like you get with some headphones in this price range.

Battery life is 5 hours per charge and you can recharge twice with the included carrying case. That's good for "true wireless" headphones.

I would give these headphones 5 stars if the sound quality was better. It does have good business features and those are the main focus of this product. Bluetooth connection is very solid and build quality is great. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case

Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black So I wanted to get some mileage on this bag before posting my review. I have had this bag now for almost 6 months and have used it regularly.
I like the overall design of the bag, it has held up nicely, wasn't super expensive and took the weight of a backpack off my back (so a plus for those of us who have back issues).

It has 3 zippered sections to put your things in. The first zippered section on the front has 2 pen pockets, 2 small pockets you can put pens or other things in, 4 business card pockets with a pocket the runs behind the business cards and 2 larger pockets that run horizontal behind all of that. (Ill include pictures to help show what I am saying)

The 2nd section has a laptop pouch. I measured my laptop and its length is 15 inches and is 10 inches wide/tall when in pouch, but it is a 17 inch screen (horizontal measurement of laptop for those who don't know). The pouch is has a little bit of padding on the front and back, so your laptop is safe there. The bottom seems okay as well and my computer has not suffered any damage, but for some who are more particular about their tech, you may want just a thin layer of foam or other cushioning (depending on the size of the laptop, you may can it in a sleeve into the pouch). There is also room to put some files or a binder in this section as well.

The last section is large enough to fit a 3 ring binder in, though you might fit a larger one if you don't have anything in the center section. The inside measurements are 13 inches tall from bottom to under the zipper and 15 inches wide from inside corner to inside corner. The dimensions listed in the product description say 17 (tall) x 14.5 (long) x 7.5 (wide)

Moving along to the wheels and handles. The wheels seem pretty sturdy so far and I have not had any trouble from them. They also are not swivel, so this may be a no go for someone looking for a bag with swivel wheels. The cloth handle is sturdy and nice to have when having to lift the bag out of your vehicle or going up stairs. The extended handle has a little loose feeling (and may feel cheap if you have owned a more expensive bag, but from my understanding of others reviews of more expensive bags, this seems to be a common complaint about the extend handles), but from my experience with it, it has served me well and has not given me any trouble. Also I am 5'5 and the handle is just right. My supervisor has the same bag and he is probably around 6'5 and the handle extends out far enough for him too.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Rolling Laptop Case, Black

Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black) I never owned a tablet or a smartphone so I suppose if I did my review might be different but I think this is a pretty neat little tablet and the price is pretty great too.

I've had it for a couple of days and downloaded the Amazon App store which has most of the apps anyone could need. I mean seriously how many apps does an average person really use? I have downloaded quite a few games for both myself and my kids, the Kindle app, I heart Radio app, and the US newspaper app. So far its holding all of it but I also ordered a microsdhc card for extra space to hold more apps and e-books. I have a regular Kindle that I've had for quite a few years and I am able to transfer most of the books onto this tablet also (I haven't tried downloading all of them since my son uses a few for school). It has where you can calibrate the stylus. Also if you longpress the stylus onto the wallpaper it will let you change the wallpaper in the background.

It does not come with a camera and flashplayer is not installed (but what I understand you can install a "lite" version of flashplayer which I have not done as of yet). The touchscreen is more geared toward using the stylus (which is included) which is a let down to some people. You can use your fingertip but it isn't as responsive as with the stylus IMO. It also comes with a sleeve (that has a place for your stylus) and earphones. There is a charger and a USB cable. There is another cable which I'm not sure exactly what its for (sorry). I haven't used the other cables just yet (except the charger of course). As for battery life it does seem like it runs down pretty quickly (perhaps 3-4 hours). Of course, that may change depending on the type of apps you have running. I know a lot of people worry about reading books from this rather than the Kindle type e-ink. I, personally, like reading at night before I go to sleep and with the Kindle I had to keep a lamp on just to see the page..(barely)...whereas this isn't like that (my eyes are much happier!) You can change the brightness of the screen if you are worried about the brightness bothering your eyes.

I have my email accessible to the Coby Kyros so I can check it throughout the day since my daughter takes off with my laptop quite often. I also downloaded the Dolphin mini browser which I like better than the browser sent with the Kyros. It comes with the GetJar app store which has quite a few apps but Amazon has more.

Of course, I cannot guarantee how well it will hold up because I've only had it for a couple of days but overall its a nice simple little tablet. I've seen the reviews of more expensive tablets and I don't want to spend $400 on a tablet that's rated two stars. I was willing to take the chance and so far I'm happy with my purchase. I rated it 4 stars because the speaker is kinda crappy...I haven't tried listening to the radio with earphones...hopefully it sounds better. And also I wish that it was easier to install flash (I've been looking on the internet but it seems like you have to be really a techie to do it...and I'm not!) It's not an Ipad (or Ipod) so you can't rate this tablet against a product like that (of course it's half the price of a Ipod touch).
text_fidelity_b: Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Adjustable Tablet/iPad Mount Holder for Microphone and Music Stand, Black So when I ordered this mount, it was based on the title description and one small photo. Here's what I've learned since.

It's meant to be mounted to a post like what might be a part of a monitor stand. So the clamp is the shape of a hook. It does not clamp well onto flat surfaces. I wanted to mount this onto a shelf board, so I've got a plastic tube inserted on the hook side to occupy space to help it sit flat.

The holders are not spring loaded. Each end is tighten by a knob. The knobs can be difficult to access depending on the orientation of the arm. In my case one of the knob was right up against the arm. So you don't just walk up and slide you tablet into this, it needs to be set up.

The rounded retainers are plastic, not rubber. So you can't just have them on both sides. The have to be on the top or bottom or in opposing corners.

As a tablet it holder, it works. But there are far more user friendly designs out there.

I hope you found this review a little bit helpful. Thank you for reading.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Adjustable Tablet/iPad Mount Holder for Microphone and Music Stand, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fire TV Stick with Voice Remote This product has a lot of promise, but fails to deliver in some areas, and is just plan not user friendly in others.
My experience on this product was that it arrived a day late, and when it arrived it would not work with my Visio High Definition Television. The TV either did not recognize it or it did not recognize my TV. So I dragged another High Definition Television into the room that I had (LG) and it immediately began working. Set up was fairly simple, however some of the setup features are where my annoyance began. This device every now and again asks for codes for WiFi and other settings that were already input. Things like Hulu and Netflix ask me every now and again if I want to sign up or login as an existing user. Why does it randomly do this? My Roku remembered me, why cant this. Amazon Prime offers password protection to prevent family members or other unwanted individuals from charging content to your credit card through a six digit pin. However the only way to input that pin (other than downloading an app to your phone) is to use an awkward scroll wheel, and additionally oddly marked buttons to get through the numerous number menu options. It is a bit of a pain. The voice control feature is a waste of money, it only finds items that Amazon can charge you for. I attempted to look up Thomas the Train for my daughter which was not only available free for Prime Members but was also on Netflix and Hulu which I had and was free, instead all it would find was items that Amazon could charge for. This is a common problem with the voice command feature. This when coupled with the horrendous navigation menus and difficulty finding what you want make this a poor choice considering other options from Roku, Apple TV and others. A little more tweaking and this could be a great product.
text_fidelity_b: Fire TV Stick with Voice Remote

text_fidelity_a: Electric Compressed Air Duster & Vacuum, MECO Electric Air Blower, 4 in 1 Function Powerful 3-Gear to 90000RPM/12000PA Keyboard Cleaner, Rechargeable Cordless Air Duster for Computer/Car/Pet Hair Great little electronics duster.  Very easy to use, comes with a brush attachment and a nice little bag to keep it all in when not in use.  Used it on my key board and then went around using it on all of the gaming devices we have and it worked great! It's not for actual dusting of shelves or other items though, not that you can't try, but it doesn't work very well.  I wanted to get one of these for 2 main reasons, 1.) because I am tired of spending money on compressed air.  2.) I wanted to be able to safely dust our electronics, but also, my son collects rocks and has an entire 4-shelf bookshelf that holds oh so many rocks and a lot of times to thoroughly dust, you have to remove every rock and then put every rock back.  This is extremely time consuming and contrary to what Swiffer claims, all those dusters do is move the dust round and throw it back into the air and then re-settles where you just removed the dust from. Very frustrating.  These little blowers, while throwing the dust far away back into the air, you can blow the dust in a way where it settles somewhere else for permanent removal, we have several air purifiers throughout the house, so this helps and it blows it away from what you need it to, so that it doesn't settle right back to where you just removed it from, like a regular duster.  When I used this on the rock shelves though, there wasn't much in the way of even removing most of the dust, but that's okay, I didn't have high expectations here either.  I feel like this duster is great for electronics and well worth the money- no more compressed air cans for this gal!  Hope this review is helpful!
text_fidelity_b: Electric Compressed Air Duster & Vacuum, MECO Electric Air Blower, 4 in 1 Function Powerful 3-Gear to 90000RPM/12000PA Keyboard Cleaner, Rechargeable Cordless Air Duster for Computer/Car/Pet Hair

Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black) I live on a farm, so I spend a lot of time outside doing various things. I usually wear a pair of Skullcandy Hesh headphones, but I’m worried that constantly sweating will mean I’ll be replacing them regularly. So I was excited to check out Outdoor Tech’s Orcas, both because they are wireless and because they fit inside the ear. Less sweat all over everything, yay!

Unfortunately, the Orcas were horribly uncomfortable for me. I have small ears, so even the smallest ear tips (there are 3 sizes) were too big. It hurt to have them in for even 5 minutes. I tried them out while doing something that didn’t involve a lot of movement — weeding — and even then they kept falling out of my ears. I had to keep taking my gloves off and forcing them back in my ears. So I can’t imagine how they would stay in for anything more active. The “ear fins” are a neat idea, but again, both pairs are too big for me. I squished them in, but one shake of my head dislodged them.

Another note for the ear fins — if you have any piercings inside your ears, such as a rook or a forward helix, they won’t fit.

I did have trouble pairing the earbuds with my phone, but after tweeting to Outdoor Tech, they set me up with tech support and I had a reply within 10 minutes. (Email is support@outdoortech.com).

The sound quality was okay, nothing super great.

My main issue with the earbuds is just that they’re so uncomfortable! If you have small ears or problems wearing this type of headphones, I’d skip them. I’ll be sticking to my Skullcandys.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
HP ENVY Desktop Computer, Intel Core i7-10700, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 512 GB SSD Storage, Windows 10 Pro (TE01-1254, 2020 Model) It is an alright system if you are only going to be doing basic computing like Microsoft Office, email, and some Netflix (but maybe not all at the same time). However, at a current price of over $850 being saddle with only the onboard graphics is hardly acceptable. Second, this system is also only okay if you never plan to repair the computer if there are issues with the power supply or motherboard. If you toss out your systems when they break, then this will work. If you like to swap out the bad parts, run for the hills you do not want to be stuck dealing with the HP part store.

If you want to play any games or use programs that require a bit more heavy lifting, (design software, CAD, or anything pulling a bunch of images or rendering) or need to have several programs running at once, you are going to struggle without a graphics card.

But can't you just add your own Graphics Card, I mean it is 2020 after all? Well... while this system does have an open slot on the motherboard for the addition of a graphics card it is severely handicapped in using it. For one, it is a very small case and you will be stuck with a small form factor card, which tend to be more expensive than their standard size counterparts. Worse yet, the included system power is only 180 watts. You cannot run much past whatever is already in the system with that, so you will need to also upgrade the power supply. Here is where it gets annoying. HP not only uses their own motherboard (Baker in this system) but the motherboard uses a proprietary connection to the power supply, so you HAVE TO BUY their power supply and only theirs. There is not an adapter, I looked and looked and looked some more.

That means heading over to the HP parts store website and trying not to pound your head into a wall with how backwards and outdated their system is. If you manage to locate the ONLY 400 watt power supply that works with the baker motherboard (yes 400 watt is the biggest they make that work for this case and motherboard) you will be hit with a $125 price tag (more like $150 after tax and shipping) for a power supply that should really cost half that. Which even if it says is in stock, will likely be back-ordered. They told me I'd be lucky to see it in 2 months even if it says "instock" in the system. Because they are the only ones selling it, you have to either wait or just forget about the upgrade. If you NEED it because your current power supply isn't working, well too bad for you.

If you have hung in this far and managed to get the power supply squared away, you can start on the graphics card piece. Now here is where it gets fun, you will want to avoid the HP parts store. They have the GTX 1660ti listed but its price bounces from over $1000 (yes a grand) to around $700 for a card that is about $300 on Amazon. Due to the power supply limitations a 1660ti is as high as you are going to be able to get, which puts you on par with an entry level gaming laptop. Due to size limitations of the HP Envy case you will want to stick to a small form factor card (generally that means one fan not two, but measure first some of those single fans are still a bit long).

So between the $150 power supply (that you may never get) and the ($300 graphics card off amazon) you are looking at about $450 in an upgrade to basically keep pace with a low level gaming laptop that costs less than what you paid for the HP Envy to begin with.

Which is my biggest problem with this system and the reason for the 3 stars, because it only does what it says (so earns its 3 stars) BUT if it has any sort of hardware issue down the line or doesn't meet your needs, you are going to be stuck buying a whole new system or be left to the mercy of HPs terribly unreliable part store with its over inflated prices and unreliable delivery timetables.
text_fidelity_b: HP ENVY Desktop Computer, Intel Core i7-10700, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 512 GB SSD Storage, Windows 10 Pro (TE01-1254, 2020 Model)

Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema After trying about 10 different systems over 2 years, finally the Denon brings home the requirements. First, we are old school and enjoyed some seriously nice stereo systems in our day. But like many people we have given in over time to the newer realities, and our prime listening space is one of the smaller rooms in the home, without the space for full hifi.

Our requirements included needing a CD player that will not break after one month, bluetooth input integrated, a reasonable set of top cab speakers and the ability to integrate a subwoofer (we have the perfect location for a sub). We have been so dissapointed by all of the things we tried over the last 24 months... bluetooth speakers, standalone CD players, integrated systems, etc. Something was always a major compromise.

text_fidelity_a:
Datacolor Spyder X Pro – Monitor Calibrator. Color Calibration Tool for Monitor Display. Ensures accurate color for photographic images. Ideal for first-time users As a software developer and tech geek who also dabbles in graphic design and photography, good color calibration is an important thing to me. I find it extremely bothersome when looking at a multi-monitor setup where the colors don't match well. I originally bought a spyder 3 some years ago when I started using a 3 monitor setup with two different types of monitors (a 144hz gaming monitor in the center and two 60hz displays on the sides). While the spyder 3 worked well, it was very slow at calibrating which was frustrating when doing a multi-display setup. I think it took around 5-6 hours to do all 3 displays with the spyder 3 (Note that I was using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal, but the Spyder software was equally as slow)

Last year I replaced all my monitors with new ones which are all the same type and I actually never calibrated them because they looked pretty good from the factory and I never felt like spending the time to use the spyder 3.. but when I saw Datacolor had released a new lens-based Spyder with claims of it being much faster and more accurate I knew I had to try it.

I am reviewing the SpyderX Pro, which has the same hardware as the SpyderX Elite but has software limitations locking some features (the most important being the limited calibration options for gamma/white point/brightness). Because those settings are important to me and I have previous experience with DisplayCal, I am using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal software with the SpyderX hardware instead of the default Spyder software. (SpyderX support was just added to ArgyllCMS in the latest version 2.1.0 on 4/10/19)

I haven't done a side-by-side comparison with the older baffle based spyder 3 to say whether the lens-based spyderX is more accurate out of the box.. but I will say that the calibration looked good to me and I can vouch for the manufacturers claims that the SpyderX is much faster than the previous generations.. The SpyderX took around 15-20 minutes per display compared to 90-100 minutes per display with the Spyder3.

Overall I am pleased with the SpyderX and think it is a worthy upgrade over its predecessor.. but I would recommend using it with DisplayCal if you really want the best results Note that both ArgyllCMS and DisplayCal are both Free, Open Source Software so you don't have to pay anything extra if you want to use them... the only downside is that they are more complicated than the Datacolor software which is designed to be very user-friendly.
text_fidelity_b: Datacolor Spyder X Pro – Monitor Calibrator. Color Calibration Tool for Monitor Display. Ensures accurate color for photographic images. Ideal for first-time users

But as many have said the write speed leave a lot to be desired. If you are moving small files its plenty fast. Much faster then 2.0 drives. But if you move large files like 3 or 4 GB it starts out fast and gets slower and slower near the end. I compared writing the same 4GB file to this and a SanDisk drive. The SandDisc took 1 minute 55 seconds. This Kingston drive took 2 minutes 59 seconds, That's a huge difference! Also this drive got considerably hotter during the transfer. I believe the heat issues is what causes it to slow down near the end of a transfer.

I have to assume if you purchased a 128 USB drive you are going to transfer a lot of large files. If that is the case this may not be your best choice. But if you are storing many smaller files, this may do the trick. So in the end its just average with a big bump for the build quality, size and outer case.

SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers With crime rates going up in NYC, this is an ideal kit for anyone living in an apartment, especially if they're alone and elderly. It covers two areas most vulnerable to thieves: your window and the door, while the key chain is best for when you're coming home late at night on a dark, lonely street. Just pull the pin and the alarm screams.

Of the three items, I would say the window alarm rates highest in terms of usefulness. In fact, I wish this set came with three of them. We travel a lot, and the biggest fear we have is intruders breaking in through our high-rise window, as we have a fire escape near one of them.

The door stop is the least useful to me as a thief would have to break through one of our windows first before going through a door. My front door is already secured by locks and the other doors in our place generally remain open. I suppose we could reinforce the front door with the doorstop, but it seems like overkill. If you lived in a dorm and wanted a particular room to be off-limits, I suppose it would be useful in that case. This item reminds me of the alarm that would be set off if you used an emergency exit. As if in acknowledgement that this item won't be used as much as the others, no battery was supplied for it, unlike the others.

As for the key chain, this is one of those devices that will lay dormant for long periods (knock on wood). You'll have to remember to check and test the batteries occasionally because it will be rarely used.

Overall, for the price this set can't be beat. It feels more like a "sampler" pack, though, as it has only one of each product when multiples of each one would have been more helpful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Update: I have now tried two other brands (a coworker's, and bought another brand) of ergonomic mice that both work substantially better than the Anker version, which also cost less! I highly suggest anyone considering buying this, skip over it and look for another one that is cheaper with good reviews. It amazes me that a company with a known name can skip out on quality so much that other product that cost half as much outperform it in every way.

The Good:
Feels great to hold. More natural than a typical mouse. All the buttons are in the right places and do not require any strain to press. The wheel is in the perfect spot to be used by my middle finger, which is typically what I try to do, since I swear I already have arthritis in my point finger being under 30 years old...

The Bad: There is an obvious input delay, making this pretty terrible for anyone who grew up using computers. That no one else has mentioned this is beyond me. Side by side comparison of any of my Logitech mice and this Anker mouse makes the input delay on this mouse even more obvious. It feels like trying to use a mouse on a TV with interpolation (120 Hz, smooth motion, etc.) enabled. On top of the nearly deal-breaking latency issue, the input into the computer is inconsistent, causing the mouse to frequently skip around or miss my movements.

If you expect to play any game that requires any amount of precision or is time-based, you will regret buying this mouse. Games aside, this mouse reduces my productivity because of how unreliable the signal is, and the extra effort needed to predict the movement of the cursor due to the lag.

I tried the wired version of this mouse (a friend had it) and the input lag is not as bad, but is still there. Therefore, I advise against anyone buying this or the wired version, and suggest to instead look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White This product is a winner. The echo.system is here to stay. I was around during the early days of Internet technology working in the field. I had a knack for knowing what was going to be part of our future of technology and what was not. I still have that knack. This is an amazing product. I bought 2 of them. 1 for the living room. 1 for the bedroom. Every day they work on it from their end to give it more and more functionality meaning more things that it can do. You can pretty much hook it up to any Bluetooth speaker if you decide that you want better sound for music. I purchased speakers for each unit that were not related to Amazon in any way, just because I needed specialty products. I just have the unit you see here and not the ones with the more advanced speakers and so I cannot speak to them. But of the many many abilities it has, the ability to pull up music, TV, movies and more, some of my favorite things are the simplest. Instant forecasts anywhere in the world, timers and an alarm that you activate merely by speaking to it has really helped me in many ways. Do you want to know the time? Ask Alexa. Do you want to know today's forecast or next week's forecast? Just ask. They are meant to be on 24 hours a day and are activated by voice and so there are no lights on to bother a person when they are sleeping. I put the one in the bedroom not just to operate the television, but more of an alarm clock thing. So if I need to take a nap before my next client, wake me up in one hour. It's that easy. (Old Model) Seagate Backup Plus 1TB Portable External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (Black)(STBU1000100) This is a good standard external hard drive that is about the size of a 2.5" notebook drive in a slim case. That means that it is a bit smaller than the Seagate Expansion series.

Where I'd normally give a very standard hard drive four stars, I up this one to five because it has the small size of a true 2.5" HDD + the same expansion capabilities of the Expansion series (and similar series by other companies). This is not to say that I plan to upgrade, as I don't normally consider the upgrade to be cost effective. But you never know. And by exposing the SATA port beneath the SATA/USB bridge, one can create some other options: although it is semi-proprietary in the fact that the SATA port is sunk in and to the side too far to use in a standard hard drive dock, you can conceivably use other connectors and devices. For example, you can use a Seagate Expansion bridge on this hard drive, but you cannot use this hard drive's bridge on a Seagate Expansion without chopping away some extra plastic on the Expansion itself.

I won't bore you with transfer speeds and such, because most people looking at this will be limited by their computer and not by this drive. And I suppose you already know it if this is not the case for you.

For me, it's better to have the above options available than not, even if they're semi-proprietary - as long as they don't come at the expense of other features or size. I'd consider this one of the better 2.5" external hard drive options available today.
text_fidelity_b: (Old Model) Seagate Backup Plus 1TB Portable External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (Black)(STBU1000100)

text_fidelity_a:
Neewer 48 Macro LED Ring Flash Bundle with LCD Display Power Control, Adapter Rings and Flash Diffusers for Canon 650D,600D,550D,70D,60D,5D Nikon D5000,D3000,D5100,D3100,D7000,D7100,D800,D800E,D60 While this macro light has some middling quality issues at times, it does offer a viable, and very cost effective alternative to pricier setups.

The light comes with eight lens adapters to cover most of the common applications (49mm, 52mm, 55mm, 58mm, 62mm, 67mm, 72mm, 77mm). The adapters are plastic rather than metal which gives me some concerns about durability. I would have liked to see metal adapters since other low-price setups offer them instead of plastic.

The flash offers a continuous light setting, or a flash setting to time with your exposure. You can set it to use all 48 LEDs or just half (can select either the right or the left half).

It’s powered by a battery pack that takes 4AA batteries. The battery contacts on mine were initially out of place and would not make proper contact with the batteries. After adjusting the position of the contacts with a screwdriver, things worked fine. The screen includes a battery level indicator so you always know how much juice is left.

You can mount the control head on your camera using the hotshoe, or use it off-camera with an included stand. The stand is really light-duty but reasonably functional.

The control head screen is very easy to read. The controls allow for light output brightness adjustments with a simple plus/minus key system, and mode selection (all/half, flash, stead light). There's also a button to test the light output. The buttons are large and well-labeled as to function.

Note that this unit does not allow for delayed/second curtain synch flash.

It includes four diffusers (white, blue, yellow, clear/semi-translucent) that are easy to attach and remove (twist and lift).

I tested this with a Canon 5D mark II and the Canon L 100mm macro and had zero problems with functionality (other than the battery issue listed above).

This is not pro-quality gear but it’s also not pro-level in terms of price. It’s a great way to play around with macro lighting to see if it’s something you find helpful. The all-plastic design keeps this at the 4 star level, but I would certainly recommend it provided you don’t subject it to a lot of heavy use.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Neewer 48 Macro LED Ring Flash Bundle with LCD Display Power Control, Adapter Rings and Flash Diffusers for Canon 650D,600D,550D,70D,60D,5D Nikon D5000,D3000,D5100,D3100,D7000,D7100,D800,D800E,D60

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Friction Mount This is a highly quality well built item, and will hold in place well, but will not work for me.

First off, this is bigger than I imagined and it has a commanding presence on your dash. The rubber part is a lint collector so looks terrible against a nice black dash. The black pad and black mount are a green black and a purple black. The plastic riser mount itself was significantly less flexible than I needed, I basically could not get the Garmin to point in the direction I wanted no matter how I placed the rubber pad, because the mount does not swivel left and right at all and has fixed limits to the side. Then, the mount raises up higher than I wanted, more or less blocked good site lines. The adhesive definitely removes whatever is on your dash (vinyl protectant) on removal and leaves something behind, but it's not damaging the dash and I suspect it will clean up. The rubber base will conform to whatever shape, but it was really difficult to get a nice flush mount, because to test and form it requires a number of trials, and I had already removed the adhesive backing (no instructions)... NOTE for users, shape and place thoroughly before removing the backing.

Ultimately, this product probably does what it's intended to do if you know exactly what it is, I need something more low profile and flexible.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Friction Mount

I connected my phone to my computer and transferred music with no problem since that was stored on my phone's internal memory. This micro SD card must have been defective from the start, a waste of $35. If I had used it immediately – although I didn't 'need' it at the time, I could have returned it. Now I will find out if the company really guarantees this for 10 years.

text_fidelity_a:
Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red) I have had way too many sets of headphones. Mostly because my dog eats them if they are within reach. While I still have not found the perfect headset with these, they come pretty close.

Durability and battery Life - Way too early to tell. I'll update this after a few months.

Noise Canceling- Let’s get something straight - if you put your fingers in your ears, they will cancel noise. That's called passive noise canceling, or simply, blocking outside noise. True active noise canceling head phones are over the ear, and usually very expensive. These head phones do a pretty good job passively blocking outside noise by fitting very well to the ear and being angled correctly.

Sound - Everyone has different tastes when it comes to what they like to hear. Some headphones have good or bad ranges from high to low. But it is the quality of the range that matters. For instance, I like to hear bass, and to me there is nothing worse than a tinny am radio sound. These definitely have bass, but it's a bit muddy. The good news is I was able to adjust the equalizer on my phone to clean it up, mostly. Overall all though, for the price, the sound quality is pretty darn good.

Fit & Hold - They Fit and stay put! The best part of these headphones is they fit my ears perfectly. The part that goes around the ear has a wire going through it, unlike so many others. This allows you to mold the over ear wires exactly to you ear and they do not fall out. None of the last several sets I had do this, and it is an enormous benefit.

Controls - The are typical up and down volume and a center button that is used for on, off, hold, answer, etc. I wish the volume buttons were reversed, but that's just being picky. They announce power on, power off and connected. Sadly, they do not announce battery life.

Appearance – Meh. They are a bit big and boxy, but I don’t know how that‘s different from having white things hanging out of your ears for $200.00

Overall - I am giving this 5 starts not because they are the best headphones. I am giving them 5 starts because they check off almost all of my boxes and the price it great. So, 5 stars for overall function and price.

Note: I paid full price for these and I was not asked to review them. Also, if you like this review, please indicate so below. Thanks.
text_fidelity_b: Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I'm a huge fan of Microsoft keyboards. Never been much of a fan of their office productivity software, but when it comes to keyboards, Microsoft fits my needs to a T. I'm using the Microsoft Digital Media Pro keyboard which (I believe) was discontinued years ago. A shame, since it has so many useful features.

But out with the old and in with the new. I tried and did not care for the previous generation of ergonomic split keyboards from Microsoft. At first glance the Sculpt looked to be a better design. The divide between the two sets of keys did not appear to be as pronounced, and my hands seemed to fit the keyboard very well. Love the feel of the pad on the wrist rest area!

Installation was straightforward, although getting the items out of the box was a challenge. I was happy to see that the necessary batteries were included - nothing worse than having to go hunt for batteries before you can start to use a new device.

The keyboard feel strongly reminded me of a laptop. For some, that may be a good feature. For me it is not. The flat keys and shorter throw makes typing feel "unnatural." I know that sounds vague, but it's the best way I can describe it.

This odd feel translated itself into a much slower typing speed - cut my throughput by about half. Since I write reports for a living, that's a rather big issue.

I also could not come to grips with the function key placement, size and meager supply of ancillary keys. That's a feature I love with my current Media Pro keyboard in that I can map pretty much any of the ample number of multimedia keys to any function I choose, or even a URL. For example, to start SPSS, Excel and WP I press one key. Another single keypress also opens my browser and my Amazon cart URL (and yes, the lettering on that particular key is pretty much worn completely off from use).

Still, if I was forced to, I could live with the keyboard. I could not, under any circumstances, live with the mouse in this set. Feels poor, lacks refinement, and far less versatile than my Logitech M500. I tried my best to get used to the Sculpt mouse, but just grew to hate it the longer I used it.

Now, my opinions are certainly affected by my current choices in keyboards and mice since I've been using them for years and years. I've changed PCs at least three times, but have retained the same keyboard and mouse since they have worked so well. If you have less keyboard/mouse "muscle memory" perhaps the Sculpt will fit the bill. The build quality seems decent, and if they are as reliable as other Microsoft keyboards, it will continue to work for some time. But for me, I just can't move the approval meter past "meh" for the keyboard and "dud" for the mouse. Three stars.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

ArmorSuit MilitaryShield Screen Protector for Apple iPad Mini 1/2/3 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film I really can't say enough good things about this, especially at the price I paid on Amazon.

I'm VERY very very OCD about my screen protectors, and the unique wet application of this one makes it an absolute joy to apply and to use.

The instructions are very easy to follow, all you need is in the kit.

So you spray the spray stuff on, slide the shield around until it's where you want it, then squeegee it down and let it sit. For me, the iPad was completely useable immediately.

What's even better is, a few months later, the corners were lifting and getting some grit under them (not a flaw in the shield ... I was using this with an iPad cover whose silicone covers move a little and shove the shield up). I pulled the corners up, sprayed the solution on (they send way more than you need for one application), flicked off the grit, squeegeed it back down ... good as new!

Given the flexible nature of the film I think a lot of devices that get a lot of rubbing at the edges might get this peeling effect, but it's great how keeping that bottle of spray around lets you fix it right up. When I peeled the corner back i accidentally touched some tissue to the guard, and it stuck to it, and I thought I was done for ... but spraying the liquid solution on, the tissue let go and like I said, it went back down at the corners as good as new.

I'll absolutely be buying these for all future big electronic purchases.

text_fidelity_a:
Denon DSB-250BT Envaya Portable Bluetooth 8.25” Speaker (Black) - Lightweight, Waterproof & Dustproof | Up to 13 Hours of Battery Life | Hands-Free Phone Calling | Voice Compatibility with Siri This is a pricey Bluetooth speaker, but a high quality one so you do get what you pay for here. It’s one of my two favorite ones (the other is the Jam Heavy Metal) and outside of the Jam is far better sound quality than the several others I own. If you’re looking for something that gives you “adequate” music and can handle a splash or two, this is overkill. But if you want rich sound and insurance against big rain (or worse, a dunk in a pool), it’s probably worth moving up to this one.

Pros:
IP67, highly water-resistant. I confess, I didn’t test this by submerging it as it says you can; I’m gonna just trust ‘em on this one

Rich, distortion-free sound. Despite its size, this can get quite loud (in a nice touch for those wishing to pump it up, the volume controls on the speaker, unlike most I own, work independently of your source device (i.e. you can max out your iphone volume and then in addition max out the speaker). Even at high volume the sound doesn’t distort. And the bass is powerful and thick (not sub-woofer but then, if you want that, get a sub-woofer. For a portable speaker, it’s perhaps the best bass I’ve heard). It’s also quite clear. In comparison to the Jam, I’d say the bass on this is better but the Jam just edges out in terms of clarity with treble/voice. The sound quality is also quite good as a speaker phone.

Connecting. Pairing via Bluetooth was pretty instantaneous with my iPhone and iPad. There’s also an audio-jack to plug in

Stereo potential. You can link it with another, though I don’t have a second so can’t speak to how it sounds

Size: it’s small enough to toss easily into a backpack if not a pocket. Has a heft to it in terms of a quality, durable build-feel, but not so as to strain you carrying it around at all.

Cons are all pretty minor
Buttons are a bit stiff (maybe this will change)

No charging cable with mine

Neutral: no connectivity with voice activation like Alexa
Charges in a few hours and last anywhere from 8-12 depending on volume, not the best but far from the worst

Personally, I hate tinny, thin-sounding speakers. If I’m going to listen to music, I don’t need it to be pristine, but I do want it to sound like my music, so I think this is a good value. The sound quality alone is worth it—it blows away cheaper Bluetooth portables— and combined with the high-level water resistance, it’s makes it an even easier recommendation
text_fidelity_b: Denon DSB-250BT Envaya Portable Bluetooth 8.25” Speaker (Black) - Lightweight, Waterproof & Dustproof | Up to 13 Hours of Battery Life | Hands-Free Phone Calling | Voice Compatibility with Siri

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation UPDATED March 11, 2015--See Below

SHOULD YOU BUY THIS UNIT?
In my opinion, this unit, like all things Amazon, is only about 80% ready for market but they release this stuff anyway. It's a cheap shot to their customers and they should straighten up and actually release products when they have all the features advertised actually implemented.

Buy this thing only if USB isn't important to you AND if you are willing to wait hours to upload video and picture content to the Amazon Cloud Drive. ABOUT THE CLOUD DRIVE--the initial allocation of space for your account is only a few gigs (I think 2 gigs). After that you can upgrade and pay Amazon more money for the bump up in storage space. That this unit has a non-functioning, flaccid USB forces you to use their cloud for video streaming your own stuff and this works for Amazon because lots of folks will end up paying for more cloud storage. This is borderline unethical in my opinion.

Pros:
Sets up easily.
Great help videos
Outstanding picture quality
WiFi and Wired connections both very good
Small footprint

Cons:
USB not implemented so you cannot play your own video content without uploading to their cloud
Uploading to their Cloud takes much longer than other clouds (Dropbox for example). It's hours compared to minutes
Puny cloud storage allocation without upgrade
Search has no QWERTY layout to type in your search and no way to add a space and second or more words to the search
Limited on-line support

CONCLUSION: Not really ready for prime time if you need full functionality in a unit like this.

UPDATED March 11, 2015: REDUCING THIS TO TWO STARS. Okay, this is the most annoying, frustrating and unreliable piece of technology I've ever purchased. In the months since I bought this item its performance has degraded to where it is simply unacceptable. Amazon tech support is of little help and neither is Netflix tech support. Here are the NEW FEATURES my Fire TV now performs:

1) Regularly pauses an in-progress program as if I'd pressed the pause button. It usually resumes after I press the play button on the remote.
2) It does not play nice with Netflix and often (actually daily) gets hung so that I see an error message telling me there's trouble, "playing this video right now...," and suggests I try later or pick something different. Well, I don't want to wait, nor do I wish to watch something else.
3) It often cannot find my HDMI cable, even though I've tried several cables. It is, therefore, not a cable problem but an internal glitch in the Fire TV box.
4) Often after turning it on, it goes to a blank screen from which there is no return.
5) There are many more fun things this piece of garbage does but why bother list them.

Tomorrow, I'm going to Best Buy to pick up a Roku 3 for about what it sells for on Amazon. See, then I won't have to wait for it to be shipped and, if necessary, I can take it back to a real store and exchange or return it. Oh, and I intend to donate this Fire TV box to the garbage can. I do hope it won't offend the garbage man/woman/person/whatever.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo VMS5140-100NAS Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 1 Camera System Update: one star. Stopped holding a charge after 3 months.

These are the first security cameras we've ever used, and I was able to install them myself in about a half hour. While they do a good job recording video and saving it so I can view it on my phone, the app is lacking and there are a couple of things that I find frustrating. I'll break my review into pros and cons.

Pros:
1. Fast install
2. Rechargeable (but only one base station)
3. Can view what is going on in my house when I am not there, can talk to the dog if I see him getting into the trash
4. Backs up my videos so I can look at them later if I am not home but cannot check the notification
5. I like the option to have a light come on at night, sound a siren, or call emergency services.
6. Decent video, I don't think it's 4k HD though, and wonderful audio.

Cons
1. The battery life. It lasts about 5 days, but one of mine is mounted outside so I have to stand on a chair or ladder to disconnect it and reconnect it.
2. Only one charing base is included for two cameras. They usually die around the same time and I can only charge one, the extra chargers are pricey and it seems to be a proprietary wire.
3. It came with one magnetic mount, which I love, and another mount that is a screw and ball. This mount doesn't feel as secure and I don't get why it just didn't have two of the same ones. It looks weird having the same camera with different mounts.
3. They are 4k, IF you pay. If you don't then they record in a lower quality. I don't mind, but it's misleading how it's phrased.
4. The app is clunky. I found it hard to block out areas where I didn't need notifications (like, every car that drives by on the road). I also was overwhelmed with notifications every time someone walks through my living room. I figured out how to set the cameras to a schedule/geo-fence, but WATCH OUT! The geo-fence doesn't work if you disconnect your phone from Wifi when you leave.
5. Notifications: When I'm not home I get an alert every time my cats walk through the room, so I had to shut off notifications all together. A little frustrating, but understandable.
6. Timers. If you want the camera to run from 10pm to 5am, you have to set it for the current day 10pm-11:59 pm, then the next day from 12:01am to 5:00am. It's kind of difficult and it kept not saving it when I set it up that way so I gave up and just set it from 12:01am-5:00am.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo VMS5140-100NAS Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 1 Camera System

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th) I've been an avid fan of ebooks since the long gone days of the Rocket and the eBookman, and a fan of the Kindle since the very beginning. This is miles and away the best there has ever been. It is a luxury model, no doubt, but oh is it luxurious.

I like:
The weight. Even in the case it's very light, though if it gets much lighter I'll worry about it blowing away in a strong wind.
The size. It's not going to get much smaller without shrinking the screen.
The interface. I'm sorry, I like buttons. Call me old. I never bent back the spine of a book (horrors) so I can't compare the feel of this to that, but I can say it's nice for a long reading session. The touch screen takes a bit of getting used to, but the tutorial will guide a new user. The tutorial is intrusive at first, but provides useful information and goes away quickly. I will suggest customizing the screen. I hated the default, but you get a lot of options to make it just the way you want.
The lighting is now all but invisible. I was unhappy that you can't completely turn it off as you could with the Nook Glowlight, and turning it down casts an odd yellow light over the page, but it's so even now as to be so unintrusive I barely notice going from sunlight to tunnel on the bus home. With the Nook I'd be thrown out of the book to go turn on the light. With the Kindle, I can keep reading without a pause. It does not have adaptive lighting, but I'm not sure it needs it.
The download speed. I don't know if it's supposed to be faster than the Kindle Keyboard (the last one I had with 3G) but it certainly seems that way.
The battery life. Maybe with this thing going for months we'll finally hear an end to the "but my dead tree doesn't run out of power" nonsense.
Next in series. When you're almost done with a book, it tells you where the story continues. Now the next feature I want, and if it does this I haven't seen it yet, is an alert when the next book in a series I'm following is published. Yes, FictFact is great, but I'm greedy and want it right on the device.

I don't like:
It's not waterproof. There was a lot of hope it would be after the Nook went that route.
It's not solar, yet, but there are rumors of a solar cover coming soon.
It doesn't support Audible and the excellent immersive reading between ebook and audiobook. I have a weird love of that feature, seeing what changed print to audio.
Recommended Content and Reading Lists. I shut this feature off. The information seems scattered at best and gave me no useful information, especially considering how precious screen real estate is.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th)

With headphones, it is always a blend of "you get what you paid for", and comparing to others at a similar price point.
How do these compare? Well, they are about average for the $20-$40 range. Not much better, not much worse. And as is the case with headphones, for a bit more, you can do MUCH better, and for a bit less, you will get roughly similar results. (In other words, headphones under $75-$100 are, more or less very similar, and then suddenly, your options get drastically better.)

Here's my analysis on the general sound quality and other features:

MISC:
Phone calls: 5 stars: Easy to use, works great for calls on both ends, and blocks outside sound quite well!
Ease of use/pairing: 5 stars: It passed the test of not having to read instructions, meaning it is incredibly simple to pair and use
Appearance: 5 stars: Neat! It's colorful and fun, as well as practical and functional!
External noise: 4 stars: Because it has a pretty tight seal, it is like an earplug, blocking outside sound quite effectively
Comfort: 3 stars: comparable to others of this design. Totally fine at first, and annoying after long use.

SOUND:
Treble: 2 stars: quite tinny
Bass: 2 stars: ok depth, not great, not very powerful
Overall: 2 stars: not much detail in the sound, but it can get pretty loud without distorting, and it is definitely good enough for basic listening and phone calls. There also appears to be a *very slight* hiss in quiet/silent moments when the volume is louder.

OVERALL:
The average is 28 out of 40 possible points, or 70% (a "C" grade, if it were going to school ;-), but because the above analysis does not take price point into account, comparing this to brands like Bose, as well as dollar store headphones, this means that for the current list price of roughly $29.99, this is a reasonable expectation.

The average number of stars based on my rubric is 3.5 stars: decent for this price point, and certainly good enough to enjoy music and spoken word, and to have successful phone calls.
text_fidelity_b: JVC Soft Wireless Earbud with Stayfit Tips, Remote and Mic and Bluetooth Violet (HA-FX9BTV)

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel I'm an early adopter of lots of "smart everything" internet connected products (Nest stuff, Smart Grill, SmartVents, internet connected cars, etc.). I have found the Ring doorbell to be one of the most useful and reliable of these types of products. Remote functions that are really valuable to me:
* Remotely "greet" and reschedule the delivery guy who was 2 hours late, while you are out doing other other errands. Warning - it does really freak out most delivery guys to hear your voice emanating from the doorbell button !
* Receive confirmation that your tween/teen has made it home from school, even when they don't see fit to call or text. Plus do a body count to see if any "extras" are visiting. Plus also have a concrete, time-stamped log of any late night returns, so you don't have to stay up late to intercept returning teens.
* Capture video evidence of stolen packages, unwanted solicitations, and prowlers.
The cloud recording cost of 30$/yr is a far better value than other services like Next or Flir. Ring is the clear choice for door monitoring as well as a really cool doorbell.

My only caveats for buyers:
* Take care with the physical installation on very rough surfaces like rough stucco. Holes need to exactly align (no slotted mounting holes) plus the mount plate is sensitive to bending. If the most bends too much to conform to the wall, the actual button/bell unit will not attach.
* Make sure your WiFi signal is strong enough in the location where you are planning install the ring. Plaster and stucco (with embedded screening) attenuate WiFi signals. WiFi basestation with beam-forming really do help (one of my neighbors needed to swap an Apple Airport Express for an Airport Extreme Basestation to achieve reliable and no-laggy video, but now the Ring works like a charm)
* Make sure your transformer is putting out an in-spec voltage, for a wired installation. Mine worked fine, but the another neighbor who recommended the Ring to me wen through two units (replaced by Ring), before they determined the doorbell voltage from the transformer was too high. Things worked flawlessly with the third unit when my neighbor moved to unwired operation.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell (1st Gen) – 720p HD video, motion activated alerts, easy installation – Satin Nickel
