text_fidelity_a:
Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507) Overall, this is a decent full-size USB keyboard. The keys are nicely sized and have a medium length throw. There’s little tactile feedback, making the keys feel rather mushy. But, on the plus side, it’s 100% silent in use – no clicky sound of any type.

The layout is a standard QWERTY with a separate number key pad and F1 to F12 at the top. There’s also a separate pad for cursor up/down/right/left.

The back light is very nice and has the unique feature in that you can change the color. There are several to pick from including a “mixed” mode that has several colors making for a rainbow look. Color selection is easy via a dedicated key at the top of the keyboard. Just press it to cycle through the colors. The back light can also be set to off.

The build quality is decent. It’s all plastic and pretty lightweight, but durable enough for normal use. There’s a kick stand on the back that folds out to prop up the keyboard at a comfortable angle, and non-skid feet to hold it in place. I had no problems with this staying put even when banging away at full typing speed. There is some flex in the frame when typing with force, but nothing horrible.

There’s a small area for resting your palm, but it’s rather short to provide much (if any) ergonomic support.

It does not have any indicator lights such as for caps lock, num lock, etc.

Installation is simple on a Win machine -- just a plug-and-play with no drivers needed.

While the overall design is nice and I love the back light feature (plus the ability to change colors), the lack of tactile feel and the lack of status indicator lights drops my rating to 4 stars. Still well worth considering as a replacement full-size USB keyboard, especially if you’re looking for a 100% silent keyboard.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507)

Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I wish I could say I loved this Fire as much as I did my original one. I thought I was upgrading to more power, more space, etc., but while some things improved, I've paid for it with truly horrible battery life. When I'd had it for less than a year, I started losing the charge at an accelerated rate. I tried turning off the wi-fi when I wasn't using the tablet, and that did help a bit, but it seemed as if everything I did was a huge drain. Surf the web for half an hour and I've lost 20% of my charge. Play a couple of games, another 20% (and not graphics intensive games either!) Yeah I can keep the wi-fi off, and turn off the tablet and not lose much at all, but what's the point of having a tablet then?

I contacted Amazon, and was told I'd have to to a complete system reset. The only thing this really accomplished, apart from a short space in which the charge lasted a little bit longer, was that I automatically got back all the apps I'd deleted because I didn't like them. So that was time wasted removing them from my system.

Nope, not happy. This Fire is only a bit over a year old, and I can't rely on it for anything but at-home use because I never know how long the battery will last.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth) Had a STR-DN1040, which we liked. Had no problem getting it up and running in our dedicated home theater. It worked well and sounded great. However, after 8 months the HDMI board went out (common problem we've learned). It was still under warranty, so we sent it off to Sony. Sony was not going to have the parts available for more than a month, so they offered us a brand new STR-DN1050. Sony customer service was excellent and it's hard to knock them when they offer a brand new amp that is the next newer model. We only received the new amp this week, but so far we love it. It was easy to set up and get running. I like the on screen setup display for the amp. It was very easy to navigate through. I know that several reviews I read complained about their being fewer HDMI inputs than the 1040. To us that did not matter as it is in a dedicated media room that only has a Blu-ray, DirecTV, and an iPhone connected to it. It sill has the front HDMI in the event we want to make an impromptu addition, as well more rear HDMI inputs available. I also read about folks complaining that the remote controls less functions. I am content with the new remote, as I didn't really control everything from the stock remote anyway. We really like that when we turn up the volume on the new remote, a volume control is displayed on the video screen. The 1040 did not do that and we missed it since our previous Onkyo did. There were also some concerns that the AMP was not truly 4K compatible. We use an Epson 8350 1080p projector (http://www.amazon.com/Epson-PowerLite-Home-Cinema-Projector/dp/B0044UHJWY/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1426790549&sr=8-1&keywords=Epson+8350), so not having full 4K compatibility is not a problem. To us the Blu-ray and DirecTV HD programs look awesome.

For a mid-range/price I would absolutely recommend this amp. Of course you can spend more, but why? Since the last amp went out after 8 mos, I am going to leave this review with 4 stars until we get some time under it's belt.

If you want to make your life and set up so much easier, also get the Deadbolt Banana Plugs, 12-pair, By Sewell Direct: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B006U3O566/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
text_fidelity_b: Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)

Mudder Portable USB Light Laptop Light for Keyboard Flexible Stick Dimmable Touch Switch LED White Light Lamp for Laptop Computer PC (Black) This is one of those simple but really useful gadgets to have. It's an LED light but, instead of a single bulb or two, it has a row of 10 bulbs arranged in a 6 inch span. The light output at it's brightest level is very bright - actually too bright in that you'll hurt your eyes if you look at the bulbs when they are at full brightness.

You turn the light on by tapping the end of the "bulb stick." Touch once to turn it on/off, press and hold while it is on to adjust the brightness. There's a wide range of brightness levels, from ultra bright to barely on. Unfortunately, it does not remember the last setting when you turn it off and then turn it on again. It always comes on at the brightest setting.

The stalk is very bendy but holds its position well. It's also very sturdy, with a metal rather than plastic casing. The total length is about 19 inches; the bendable stalk about 10.5 inches long. This is very thin - the bulb end is about the width of a pencil - so it's easy to fold up and stow in a tablet or laptop bag. Excellent build quality, especially considering the price.

It has a standard USB connector on the end for power. I've been powering it with a small powerbank and it draws very little power - leaving it on for several hours barely made a dent in the powerbank charge level.

I find this very helpful when using a tablet at night. I can bend the stalk so the light shines where I want it (the attached keyboard) but not on the screen. It's easy to stow when not in use - no wires or bits that get tangled up. Great value for the price.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Mudder Portable USB Light Laptop Light for Keyboard Flexible Stick Dimmable Touch Switch LED White Light Lamp for Laptop Computer PC (Black)

The Elite 3's pretty much behave for me like the Active 75t's. They both fit in my ear fantastically and stay there. They both have exceptional sound quality. They both charge easy and keep a great charge. The case feels cheaper with these newer 3's and the earbud itself feels cheaper. Cheaper, but at the same time lighter which is a good thing. The color offerings are also not as good as the Active 75t's were. With those, I have a color called "Sienna" which is a golden peachy color and kinds really compliments my skin tone and so those earbuds don't stand out. THESE earbuds are dark grey, one of 4 colors offered and just look like standard earbuds in color.

I think the main difference between the two is the active 75ts are more designed to be waterproof, sweatproof, and for sports. THESE Elite 3's are more basic.

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling I've had the opportunity to review three different G.G. Martinsen players, and of the three this one is my favorite. I brought two of the players, pre-charged, to review at my sister's where I am staying a week while she had and recovers from surgery, and the one thing I can say right off the bat is that I wish the charging cable was of the ubiquitous Micro-A type and not the mini type, which I did not think to bring with me. The [[ASIN:B016F4AGLC other player]] handles like the [[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ first one]] I reviewed for G.G. Martinsen, but I will have to wait until I get back home to do anything other than test the recorder and FM radio on this 16GB player because I have no cable to copy music onto the player with!

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa "Set up in minutes"?? Not really. There are no actual detailed instructions included. I tried scanning the QR code that was provided in the little pamphlet, and that was not helpful. This ended up being extremely frustrating to set up. I could take a wild guess that I was supposed put the lithium batteries in the back of the camera. I would not have known that the little QR code inside the camera where the batteries go was something that I had to scan to set up the camera. Anyway, without going into detail, if Amazon provided some simple, basic instructions with photos that show step by step, it would save the customer a ton of fumbling around. Then it might have been an easy set up. I had to call for support, and by the time I got a support person on the phone I was pretty irritated. The reason I decided to buy this camera is the "two-year battery life." Note: these are not rechargeable batteries. We'll see how long the batteries last. Prior to this, I got a Eufy Solocam, also wireless (and much, much easier to set up), and it had rechargeable batteries advertised to last 4 months, but they lasted 4 weeks. A feature that is missing with the Blink camera, that I liked on the Eufy camera, is the AI feature to recognize humans. Without the AI feature, the Blink is recording non-human motion, such as animals and vehicles.

Update: The description advertises customized zones for motion detection. The camera takes a photo what it sees, and in motion settings, you gray out areas that you do not want the camera to detect motion. It does NOT work. I tried resetting it several times, and the camera recorded and sent me an alert of motion detected that was squarely in the grayed out area. Without this feature actually working, and without the AI feature to detect humans, the camera is recording every motion in the entire viewable area, ignoring the areas that I grayed out. I am returning this camera.
text_fidelity_b: Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black Very good headphones. Smallish ear pieces and the black plastic shell is not real attractive, but they feel solid and well made. Rubber ear tips are comfortable for long periods of time and 3 different sizes of replacement tips are included. Bass is very good and overall sound clarity is much better than with cheap headphones. Full volume is more than loud enough for me and distortion at the highest volume is tolerable (unlike with cheap headphones). Wrap-around cables can be a hassle, but these have thicker wires and don't tangle as much as others that I have tried. Wrap-around cables really prevent the earbuds from falling out when I am working out. A simple nylon bag is the only carrying case included in the oversized box, but better cases are available at dollar stores.

Yes, Apple is trying to kill off wired headphones, but wired headphones still have huge advantages over Bluetooth, such as not having to worry about battery life, being able to recharge your phone at the same time you are listening to music, and of course the sound quality of wired headphones is usually better than similarly priced Bluetooth headphones.

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL) As a long-time Apple user, I am strongly considering other options because of a number of issues, including software updates that slow to a halt older devices ("planned obsolescence" is what they call it). Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

Quality: Great image on the screen with very high resolution! The feel of the device is also sturdy, aesthetically pleasing, lightweight, and thin.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL)
